title: How do you choose a zip bag and shipping mailer for a clothing drop?
seoTitle: Branded Zip Bags and Mailers for Clothing
description: Test the folded garment, seal, artwork and external size sticker before ordering branded packaging for your apparel collection.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: A garment zip bag presents an individual item and keeps its variant identifiable. An outer shipping mailer has a different job: it carries the packed order through dispatch. Choose each using the actual contents. A thin tee, a double-layer hoodie and a boxed set will not necessarily suit the same bag.

toc.text: Start with a packed item at each extreme
Make the size visible before anyone opens the bag
How do you check whether a bag sticker survives normal handling?
Check what happens to an actual order

bodyHtml:
Start with a packed item at each extreme

Fold the smallest and largest garments the way the packing team will fold bulk. Include hangtags, tissue or other inserts that will really be used. Slide the largest piece into the proposed inner bag, close it and set it down overnight if practical. A bag that closes only while someone is compressing the hoodie can be difficult to pick and repack.

For the smallest piece, look at the presentation through the front. Does the garment slip so far that the logo disappears? Check the outer mailer separately with a typical single-item order and a realistic multi-item order.

Make the size visible before anyone opens the bag

For identical boxer shorts sold in several sizes, put the correct size sticker on the outside of each sealed pack. Decide on one consistent position, clear of the closure and the main artwork. A picker should be able to select size M from a carton without opening a bag. Have someone who did not pack the order read the sticker, open a test pack and compare it with the label sewn into the garment.

Packing checkpointEvidence to retain
Fold and orientationFront and back photos of one approved pack
Variant identificationSize or SKU on the exterior matched to the garment inside
ArtworkLegible wordmark with the bag filled and closed
DispatchOuter mailer closes and leaves room for the carrier label

How do you check whether a bag sticker survives normal handling?

Pack a representative garment, close the bag and put it into the shipping carton in the intended orientation. Remove it again as a picker would. Check whether the sticker stayed on a flat, visible surface and whether a barcode, if used, still scans. Repeat with the largest folded garment if the fold pushes against the label area.

Check what happens to an actual order

Pack two different sizes for the same customer. Scan or read the variants, seal the mailer and open it as a customer would. Watch for tags caught in the seal or a sticker put on a removable cover instead of the bag. Update the packing instructions with a picture of the correct result.
